title: [client-go] add a pod-logs example
body:
**What would you like to be added?** I'd like to add a new pod-logs example to [INLINE_CODE]. It's a simple script that lists pods across namespaces and streams the last few lines of their container logs to the terminal.

**Why is this needed?** I noticed we don't actually have a basic "how to get pod logs" example. It's such a common thing for people to do, but there isn't a dedicated example yet!

I've based this on the official [Python client's logs example](https://github.com/kubernetes-client/python/blob/master/examples/pod_logs.py).

**Why is this needed?** I noticed we don't actually have a basic "how to get pod logs" example. It's such a common thing for people to do, but there isn't a dedicated example yet!

I've based this on the official [Python client's logs example](https://github.com/kubernetes-client/python/blob/master/examples/pod_logs.py).

title: Graduate old Alpha metrics to Beta
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Before introduction of Beta metric stability, we had many important metrics that were stuck in Alpha state.

Would like to propose a list of metric candidates that should be reviewed for graduation to Beta.

We would still review each metric individually for any antipattern, but fact they are in use for so long should be good enough reason for graduation. 

Graduation criteria are at https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/9de615daee15bdee370a825dc0ef150eac189700/contributors/devel/sig-instrumentation/metric-instrumentation.md#graduating-to-beta

Subtasks:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136304
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136305
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136306
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136307
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136308
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136310
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136311
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136312
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136313

### Why is this needed?

Those metrics have been already present in K8s for long time and are at use by GKE. 

While we won't necessarily want to graduate them GA, marking them as Beta would indicate their importance and allow community to pay more attention to them over other Alpha metrics.

/cc @richabanker @dgrisonnet

similar_issues.text: Policy for metric graduation and timely removal of deprecated metrics. * * problem * * : we currently have a significant number of metrics that are stuck at [ alpha ] ( https : / / kubernetes. io / docs / reference / instrumentation / metrics / # list - of - alpha - kubernetes - metrics ) ( 450 as of v1. 34 ) and [ beta ] ( https : / / kubernetes. io / docs / reference / instrumentation / metrics / # list - of - beta - kubernetes - metrics ) ( 23 as of v1. 34 ) stability levels, as well as deprecated metrics ( 8 as of v1. 34 ) that have not been removed according to our deprecation timeline. this creates several issues : 1. user uncertainty : users maybe wary of relying on alpha / beta metrics for production monitoring and alerting, yet many of these metrics have been at these levels for multiple releases 2. technical debt : deprecated metrics that linger beyond their expected removal timeline add maintenance burden and potential confusion 3. lack of accountability : there is no clear ownership or process to ensure metrics progress through their lifecycle we need some way of ensuring the following preferably by automation 1. graduation tracking 1. metrics at alpha for more than n releases should either : 1. graduate to beta ( with required testing ) 2. be deprecated and removed 2. metrics at beta for more than m releases should either : 1. graduate to stable ( with required testing and api review ) 2. be deprecated 2. deprecation enforcement 1. implement tooling / automation to identify metrics that have exceeded their deprecation timeline 2. create a release - blocking mechanism or regular audit process to ensure deprecated metrics are removed on schedule 3. ownership 1. each metric should have a clear owning sig responsible for its lifecycle 2. periodic reviews ( e. g., quarterly ) to assess metric status * * questions * * 1. what should be the maximum time a metric can remain at alpha before requiring action? 2. what should be the maximum time a metric can remain at beta before requiring action? 3. should we have exceptions for certain categories of metrics? 4. how do we handle metrics where the owning component / sig is unclear? title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Readiness Observations & Recommendations (Research)
body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue shares research-based observations on post-quantum cryptography (PQC) readiness
in Kubernetes, based solely on publicly available code and documentation.

This is NOT a vulnerability report and does not include exploitation, attack paths, or
sensitive configuration details. The intent is awareness, future-readiness, and community
discussion aligned with NIST PQC transition guidance.

Observations:
• Cryptographic usage is distributed across multiple layers
• There is no centralized crypto inventory or ownership map
• No defined crypto agility or PQC migration framework
• No governance-level visibility into algorithm lifecycle

Recommendations:
• Consider adding a crypto inventory layer
• Define crypto ownership and lifecycle policy
• Track NIST PQC migration readiness
• Introduce crypto agility abstractions
• Document PQC roadmap for operators

Why this matters:
Quantum-safe transitions are multi-year efforts. Early visibility reduces long-term risk.

Happy to refine or contribute to documentation if helpful.

### Why is this needed?

Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) transitions are multi-year efforts that require early visibility and planning. 
Today, Kubernetes uses strong cryptography, but cryptographic usage is distributed across many layers 
(control plane, components, SDKs, dependencies), making long-term migration and governance difficult to track.

This enhancement is needed to:
- Improve visibility into cryptographic usage and ownership
- Enable crypto agility and algorithm lifecycle management
- Align Kubernetes with NIST post-quantum transition guidance
- Reduce future migration risk by identifying readiness gaps early
- Support operators and maintainers with clear, documented PQC readiness signals

This is not related to an exploitable vulnerability. 
It is a forward-looking readiness and governance improvement to help Kubernetes remain secure over the next decade.

body_raw:
### What would you like to be added?

Building with a more vanilla setcap image shouldn't require a shell in the image to run the command 


in `build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile`

```sh
# We apply cap_net_bind_service so that kube-apiserver can be run as
# non-root and still listen on port less than 1024
RUN setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /${BINARY}
```

this command requires the `SETCAP_IMAGE` have a shell in order to:
1) RUN a command that isn't in the form of ["/usr/sbin/setcap", "..."] 
2) shell expand the `${BINARY}` argument


### Why is this needed?

By making this change you can eliminate the need of having a shell in the setcap image:


```diff
diff --git a/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile b/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
index 27129d29bd9..acfe8c26f22 100644
--- a/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
+++ b/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
@@ -20,11 +20,11 @@ ARG SETCAP_IMAGE
 # to setup qemu for the builder.
 FROM --platform=linux/$BUILDARCH ${SETCAP_IMAGE}
 ARG BINARY
-COPY --chmod=755 ${BINARY} /${BINARY}
+COPY --chmod=755 ${BINARY} /set_cap_binary
 # We apply cap_net_bind_service so that kube-apiserver can be run as
 # non-root and still listen on port less than 1024
-RUN setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /${BINARY}
+RUN ["setcap", "cap_net_bind_service=+ep", "/set_cap_binary"]
 
 FROM --platform=linux/$TARGETARCH ${BASEIMAGE}
 ARG BINARY
-COPY --from=0 /${BINARY} /usr/local/bin/${BINARY}
+COPY --from=0 /set_cap_binary /usr/local/bin/${BINARY}
```

title: Metrics monitors getter set by DefaultStorageFactory is being overwritten by SimpleStorageFactory
body:
### What happened?

I investigated an issue with etcd storage metrics collection where etcd overrides weren't appearing correctly in the metrics.

Expected behavior: According to the ([implementation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/metrics/metrics.go#L331)) and ([original intention](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118812#discussion_r1252695238)), etcd overrides should be configured separately and displayed as etcd-1, etcd-2, etc.

Actual behavior: Only etcd-0 (the base etcd server) appeared in metrics, even when overrides were configured.

Likely Root cause: The monitor getter (which retrieves etcd configs) is set twice:

First by DefaultStorageFactory (includes overrides map)

Then by SimpleStorageFactory (excludes overrides map)

Since the monitor getter is a global variable, the second call overwrites the first. All subsequent monitor retrievals use SimpleStorageFactory's configuration, which lacks the etcd overrides.

I was able to solve this in local testing by restricting monitor getter updates to only DefaultStorageFactory (used by the main kube-apiserver with overrides). Preventing SimpleStorageFactory from overwriting it. Not sure if this is a complete fix.

modify [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go#L243) to 
[CODE_BLOCK]

#### kube-controller-manager log:
```

The issue was the "requestURI": `/apis/batch/v1/jobs/sleep-300-job-29512485` is correct, it should contain `namespace` e.g.:
```
❯ kubectl get job sleep-300-job-29512485 -v 9                                      
...
I0210 18:52:07.314585   31290 round_trippers.go:632] "Response" verb="GET" url="https://192.168.130.2:8443/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/default/jobs/sleep-300-job-29512485" status="200 OK" headers=<
```

And the API Server's 404 indicated there's no `/apis/batch/v1/jobs/` API.

### What did you expect to happen?

Cronjob controller should query the job `with namespace`:

Incorrect URI (current):
```
/apis/batch/v1/jobs/<JOB_NAME>
```

Correct URI:
```
/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/<NAMESPACE>/jobs/<JOB_NAME>
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a cronjob to create a job every 5 minutes:
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: sleep-300-job
spec:
  schedule: "*/5 * * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: echo-sleep
              image: ubuntu
              command:
                - /bin/bash
                - -c
                - echo start && sleep 180 && echo end
          restartPolicy: Never
```

Once the first job was created, create another job manually with the next expected job name (id + 5):
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: sleep-300-job-29512465
  namespace: default
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: batch/v1
    blockOwnerDeletion: true
    controller: true
    kind: CronJob
    name: sleep-300-job
    uid: d10ff40f-be9d-47d2-aa67-7a376f054ed2
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - command:
        - /bin/bash
        - -c
        - echo start && sleep 180 && echo end
        image: ubuntu
        name: echo-sleep
      restartPolicy: Never
```

Check the kube-controller-manager and API Server audit log for the result.

### Anything else we need to know?

The issue seems to be when Cronjob controller trying to get job, it used the `jobReq` from `getJobFromTemplate2()` function, however, `getJobFromTemplate2()` won't set the job Namespace:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/65f09e605cb206b2e5fcff4d69a4ae8acf62dbc3/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L621
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/65f09e605cb206b2e5fcff4d69a4ae8acf62dbc3/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L604
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/cronjob/utils.go#L256-L263

Seems we're not relying on the `namespace` from `getJobFromTemplate2()`, it seems the correct way to specify `namespace` should be the same as:
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/65f09e605cb206b2e5fcff4d69a4ae8acf62dbc3/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L609

title: Unblock enablement of the ConcurrentWatchObjectDecode by default (to fix scale issues for CRDs)
body:
### What would you like to be added?

[ConcurrentWatchObjectDecode](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/features/kube_features.go#L1955C18-L1957) is currently Beta, but disabled by default.

**I would like to identify or understand the blockers for graduation (if any) so that this can be moved forward.**

This feature gate looks very promising for handling CRD objects with high cardinality, like Workload objects in [Kueue](https://kueue.sigs.k8s.io/). Without this feature gate migration between versions like [INLINE_CODE] to [INLINE_CODE] is risky at scale.

We would love to have this improved before migrating Kueue v1beta2 -> v1.

### Why is this needed?

In Kueue 0.15 we introduced v1beta2 for serving, while keeping v1beta1 for storage. Which was dictated by the needs of downgrading to 0.14 in case something "goes wrong".

However, this caused issues on high scale clusters (small clusters <10k work fine).

My understanding of the problem:
1. when Kueue is starting up then controller-runtime tries to establish the WATCH on the Workload object in v1beta2
2. If the API server does not have a "warm" cache for the Workloads, then it requests ETCD for the list of Workloads in v1beta1
3. API server receives the workloads list, but before returning to Kueue it tries to convert them sequentially to v1beta2. 

**Issue**: for some larger clusters it was estimated to take around 8min, but this exceeds some timeouts in ETCD to serve the request, and the API server fails with 500 in the meanwhile.

There is a good chance that enabling parallel requests would save the request.

**Mitigation**: we recommend users to move from Kueue 0.15 to 0.16 (which is using v1beta2 for storage and serving) which mitigates the problem, but the situation is not ideal, because 0.15 remains affected.

Related issues in Kueue:
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/9094
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/9145
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/issues/9090

Removing dependence on PrevKV when watch cache is enabled. # # # what would you like to be added? when watching from etcd, apiserver sets [ inline _ code ] flag so the returned watch events include information about previous version. this is used by apiserver to handle watch with selector, where it needs to be aware of what were fields / labels of previous object to notice changes. this is always done on etcd3 layer. when watch cache is enabled, the watches to etcd3 never include those selectors as they are handled by cache and prevkv is replaced with value from cache. this allows us to deallocate the object, but only after it was decoded on etcd3 layer. i would propose to stop setting prevkv when watch cache is enabled. pros : * reduces lock contention in etcd mvcc by reducing number of reads by 50 % and increases write throughput by 20 % ( from https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / pull / 131862 ) * watch no longer will break when there is a missing prevkv field. etcd doesn't guarantee prevkv as the field is filled just before sending event and can race with compaction. * doubles capacity of watch stream, which was proved that can be overloaded with bad consequences. https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 123448 * halfs allocations needed to handle watch events. cons : * complicates watch code as it creates special cache for watch cache / cc @ wojtek - t @ deads2k # # # why is this needed? presented benefits are nice, so i think we might want to consider it, however i don't think there is a strong " need ". would need to measure the direct impact of reducing watch reintializations due to prevkv, reducing allocations and watch capacity problem.

Enable event watch cache by default. # # # what would you like to be added? currently, apiserver disable event watchcache by default. we did this to make test faster. see https : / / github. com / kubernetes / perf - tests / issues / 561. we could disable it in tests, but keep it enabled in the default settings. # # # why is this needed? watchcache is critical in reducing etcd pressure. we have ran into some serious issue due to lack of event watchcache. we used to have a failure rate over 80 % in a proction cluster with 14k nodes and 560k pods. with watchcahe enabled, the failure rate droped to near zero.! [ image ] ( https : / / github. com / user - attachments / assets / cb9f9472 - ce15 - 4b05 - ae32 - a440e0154cfa ) the same thing happended to request lantency.! [ image ] ( https : / / github. com / user - attachments / assets / aa836747 - 9365 - 44c5 - b7d3 - 620f1f58d1fe ) the etcd is really not good at handling large range requests. without watchcache, the list / watch goes directly to etcd, which cause a serious lock contension. we saw some large range requests took over 1m and kept hodling the lock, while others starved.! [ image ] ( https : / / github. com / user - attachments / assets / 570ca431 - 3710 - 499f - 8087 - 60ff7f0d1966 )! [ image ] ( https : / / github. com / user - attachments / assets / 6abb31cd - 83b5 - 48d5 - 986d - ee51ba02c16a ) this results in watch events pending and raft pending rising. after we enabled watchcache, these issues also dispeared.! [ image ] ( https : / / github. com / user - attachments / assets / e430381f - 9b80 - 4f09 - bd22 - 2b54c38f7f22 )! [ image ] ( https : / / github.

Feature gate `UnauthenticatedHTTP2DOSMitigation` should be a configuration setting instead of a feature gate. # # # what happened? we recently developed a layer 7 load - balancing feature for kube - apiservers in our gardener project. while we tested it in a broad scope we discovered many watches which have been remotely closed by kube - apiserver. the root cause for this was [ inline _ code ] feature gate. in our l7 setup which uses istio / envoy many clients could share one http2 connection between istio / envoy and kube - apiserver. when the feature gate is activated each anonymous and each unauthorized request closes this connection and could kill the watch of several other clients. this behavior is not desired since it creates lots of disruptions for various clients. in our case istio / envoy are responsible for mitigation of http / 2 " rapid reset " dos vulnerability. the connection between istio / envoy and kube - apiserver should not be affected. this is also mentioned in pr # 121120 which implemented [ inline _ code ] feature gate > since this change has the potential to cause issues, the unauthenticatedhttp2dosmitigation feature gate can be disabled to remove this protection ( it is enabled by default ). for example, when the api server is fronted by an l7 load balancer that is set up to mitigate http2 attacks, unauthenticated clients could force disable connection reuse between the load balancer and the api server ( many incoming connections could share the same backend connection ). an api server that is on a private network may opt to disable this protection to prevent performance regressions for unauthenticated clients. deactivating [ inline _ code ] is helping us and we are happy for now. however, a feature gate is made to graduate in a future kubernetes version. this would break our layer 7 load - balancing setup. we prefer to avoid this # # # what did you expect to happen? the mitigation of http / 2 " rapid reset " dos vulnerability should be a configuration option instead of a feature gate. this config option could be enabled by default. this way, kube - apiservers deployed in a " standard " setup would still be protected while it would be also possible to deactivate it for a layer 7 load - balancing and an aggregated apiserver setup ( see # 122308 ).

Support compression for WATCH responses. # # # what would you like to be added? i propose adding compression support for watch responses in the kubernetes api server. this feature is necessary to maintain parity with the bandwidth efficiency of the legacy list method as clients transition to watchlist. the proposal includes : 1. * * compression for watch : * * implement the capability for the server to provide compressed streaming data for watch connections. 2. * * algorithm registration interface : * * introduce an interface allowing custom compression algorithms to be registered. this ensures client - go remains lightweight and does not force new mandatory dependencies on all users. 3. * * default realtime compression : * * kubernetes binaries ( e. g., kube - apiserver, kube - controller - manager, kubectl ) should include and support a realtime data compression like [ s2 ] by default to maximize throughput. [ s2 ] : https : / / github. com / klauspost / compress / tree / master / s2 # # # why is this needed? the default enablement of watchlist for clients in kubernetes 1. 35 has fundamentally changed how initial object sets are fetched. while list operations are compressed, watch operations are not, leading to a massive spike in control plane outbound traffic. # # # key impacts : * bandwidth explosion : for most clusters communicating over a network, control plane outbound traffic can increase by 5x. * scalability bottleneck : this increased data transfer is a critical blocker for the " resource size " scalability dimension proposed in [ issue # 134375 ] ( https : / / github. com / kubernetes / kubernetes / issues / 134375 ). # # # why not gzip? * performance regression : standard library gzip implementation often slows data transfer by 2x due to cpu overhead. however, modern algorithms like [ s2 ] can actually increase throughput by 2. 5x while significantly reducing volume. * breaking change risk : most clients are configured to send accept - encoding : gzip by default, but they do not expect a compressed response for watch. enabling gzip without a negotiation mechanism would break these clients. # # # comparison : performance and volume | method | compression | data volume ( lower better ) | throughput ( higher better ) | | : - - - | : - - - | : - - - |

title: Deprecate kube-dns
body:
As discussed in [the SIG Network meeting, Feb 26](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bEA0F8WddLMnQp7zUfr1rZOwRqX6g2y4kcylEcGATHo/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.h5y61o5x0g0g) and [announced on the mailing list](https://groups.google.com/a/kubernetes.io/g/sig-network/c/RCogf4OeRk0)

To do:
- [x] Confirm that we are no longer using kube-dns in CI (we aren't: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137553#issuecomment-4025802481)
- [x] Split out node-local-dns from kubernetes/dns repo (https://github.com/kubernetes/org/issues/6192, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/node-local-dns/pull/6)
- [x] Update k/community to add the node-local-dns subproject (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/8934)
- [x] Update relevant build stuff to build the [INLINE_CODE] image out of https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/node-local-dns rather than https://github.com/kubernetes/dns (https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/36856)
- [x] Remove node-local-dns from https://github.com/kubernetes/dns to avoid confusion, and leave a forwarding pointer (https://github.com/kubernetes/dns/pull/762)
- [x] Update k/community to retire the kube-dns subproject (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/8983), send follow-up email to SIG list confirming the deprecation
- [ ] Update k/website to modernize or remove references to kube-dns
- [ ] Make sure the deprecation announcement gets into the 1.37 release notes

After 1.40 ships:
- [ ] Drop all remaining kube-dns-based CI jobs (i.e., ones that set [INLINE_CODE]) from k/test-infra
- [ ] Remove kube-dns support from k/k/cluster
- [ ] Stop building new kube-dns images
- [ ] Make any other appropriate updates to k/k, k/community, and k/website (?)
- [ ] Archive the kubernetes/dns repo

Also:
- [ ] Find a new home for [the Kubernetes DNS specification](https://github.com/kubernetes/dns/blob/master/docs/specification.md)

/assign

title: Investigate capslock for dependency update analysis
body:
https://github.com/google/capslock -- Something GKE Security folks have mentioned.

> Capslock is a capability analysis CLI for Go packages that informs users of which privileged operations a given package can access. This works by classifying the capabilities of Go packages by following transitive calls to privileged standard library operations.

> The recent increase in supply chain attacks targeting open source software has highlighted that third party dependencies should not be inherently trusted. Capabilities indicate what permissions a package has access to, and can be used in conjunction with other security signals to indicate which code requires additional scrutiny before it can be considered trusted.

NOTE: https://github.com/google/capslock/blob/main/docs/caveats.md (particularly the build tags constraint, which generally applies to our Go static analysis tools)

/area code-organization
/sig security architecture

More generally I've been mulling tooling that flags things for further review:
- init() and friends
- binary data
- cgo / linkname
- ...

We rely almost entirely on hand-reviewing incoming vendor code today, with some tooling specifically to audit the dependency _graph_ but not so much the code.

This tool seems to cover some of that, with caveats.

title: ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta [FeatureGate:HPAConfigurableTolerance] test case flaking
body:
### Which jobs are flaking?

ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta
ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu

### Which tests are flaking?

Kubernetes e2e suite.[It] [sig-autoscaling] [Feature:HPA] [Slow] [FeatureGate:HPAConfigurableTolerance] [Beta] Horizontal pod autoscaling (configurable tolerance) with small scale-up, large scale-down tolerances should scale up but should not scale down

### Since when has it been flaking?

Probably since the tests were introduced.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-autoscaling-hpa#gce-cos-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta

### Reason for failure (if possible)

Here's one example of a run that flaked in the last 7 days in the upstream CI. https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta/2030195647587553280

On OpenShift CI, we are starting to see this flake as well: https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-kubernetes-master-e2e-aws-hpa/2030871476332138496

I believe the nature of what we are actually testing in this test case, will inhernetly be flaky. Configuring HPA ConfigurableTolerance to numbers like 5% down from the default 10% creates tight windows for HPA to actually actuate scale ups according to the intended behaviour since we don't actually directly control the CPU usage of the pods. Hoping there can be someway to make this test more deterministic.

### Anything else we need to know?

The test appears in both https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-autoscaling-hpa#gce-cos-autoscaling-hpa-cpu-alpha-beta
and https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-autoscaling-hpa#gce-cos-autoscaling-hpa-cpu

The test case code is here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d559a4afe7f953ba13baf5949fec92af59f4b707/test/e2e/autoscaling/horizontal_pod_autoscaling_behavior.go#L549

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig autoscaling

### What happened?

Hi, 
I am using an ext4 filesystem formatted and mounted with the prjquota.
When I create a Pod with emptyDir as shown below, the Pod fails to start after the node is rebooted.
```bash
$ kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-pod
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0
  hostUsers: false
  containers:
  - name: test-container
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Hello World && sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: test-storage
      mountPath: /mnt/temp
  volumes:
  - name: test-storage
    emptyDir: {}
EOF
$ kubectl exec test-pod -- mkdir /mnt/temp/dir
$ kubectl exec test-pod -- touch /mnt/temp/file
```
To further narrow down the issue, I made a small code change to capture the stderr output of the xfs_quota command when the error occurs, as shown below.
```diff
diff --git a/pkg/volume/util/fsquota/common/quota_common_linux_impl.go b/pkg/volume/util/fsquota/common/quota_common_linux_impl.go
index a9959662393..fa5bfc1ccd5 100644
--- a/pkg/volume/util/fsquota/common/quota_common_linux_impl.go
+++ b/pkg/volume/util/fsquota/common/quota_common_linux_impl.go
@@ -131,11 +131,11 @@ func doRunXFSQuotaCommand(mountpoint string, mountsFile, command string) (string
        klog.V(4).Infof("runXFSQuotaCommand %s -t %s -P/dev/null -D/dev/null -x -f %s -c %s", quotaCmd, mountsFile, mountpoint, command)
        cmd := exec.Command(quotaCmd, "-t", mountsFile, "-P/dev/null", "-D/dev/null", "-x", "-f", mountpoint, "-c", command)

-       data, err := cmd.Output()
+       data, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
+       klog.V(4).Infof("runXFSQuotaCommand output:\n%s", string(data))
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
-       klog.V(4).Infof("runXFSQuotaCommand output %q", string(data))
        return string(data), nil
 }
```
The relevant kubelet logs are as follows:
```text
Mar 17 21:58:08 ubuntu24-test kubelet[2984]: I0317 21:58:08.149043    2984 quota_common_linux_impl.go:131] runXFSQuotaCommand /sbin/xfs_quota -t /tmp/mounts1038897217 -P/dev/null -D/dev/null -x -f /var/lib/kubelet -c project -s -p /var/lib/kubelet/pods/91fd6e02-f0b4-45c6-a328-0fba789f2da6/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/test-storage 1048579
Mar 17 21:58:08 ubuntu24-test kubelet[2984]: I0317 21:58:08.150025    2984 quota_common_linux_impl.go:135] runXFSQuotaCommand output:
Mar 17 21:58:08 ubuntu24-test kubelet[2984]: xfs_quota: cannot set project on /var/lib/kubelet/pods/91fd6e02-f0b4-45c6-a328-0fba789f2da6/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/test-storage/file: Operation not supported
Mar 17 21:58:08 ubuntu24-test kubelet[2984]: Setting up project 1048579 (path /var/lib/kubelet/pods/91fd6e02-f0b4-45c6-a328-0fba789f2da6/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/test-storage)...
Mar 17 21:58:08 ubuntu24-test kubelet[2984]: Processed 1 (/dev/null and cmdline) paths for project 1048579 with recursion depth infinite (-1).
```

I observed that the "not supported" error occurs only when operating on the file `test-storage/file`, but not on the directory `test-storage/dir`. This may be related to the fact that the +P (project inheritance) flag can be applied to directory inodes, but not to file inodes.

In contrast, the issue does not occur on XFS, where the same Pod can be successfully created after a node reboot.


### What did you expect to happen?

Pods using emptyDir should start successfully after a node reboot when LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring is enabled.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

As described above.

title: DRA: List Types for Attributes - fix handling of update validation when the feature gate is disabled
body:
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5491
Umbrella: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/137905

As suggested in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137190#discussion_r2945671994

Similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/137899, 

In the current device allocator implementation, [_experimental_ allocator](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.0/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go) will not read a list-type attributes when the [INLINE_CODE] feature gate is disabled.

However, already-stored CEL expression in apiserver needs to be able to work even when the gate is disabled to satisfy kubernetes version skew policy in the scenario of upgrading or flipping the feature gate.

/wg device-management
/sig scheduling

body_raw:
First reported by @serathius, recently some coworkers have been having issues with the containerized builds (e.g. `make quick-release-images` or `build/run.sh make WHAT=cmd/kubectl`) with an error like:

```console
error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128
        Use -buildvcs=false to disable VCS stamping.
```

After some debugging, I found:
```console
$ build/run.sh make WHAT=cmd/kubectl GOFLAGS=-v
+++ [0410 23:29:16] Verifying Prerequisites....
+++ [0410 23:29:17] Running build command...
Go version: go version go1.26.2 linux/amd64
# cd /go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes; git status --porcelain
fatal: multi-pack-index version 2 not recognized
+++ [0410 23:29:17] Building go targets for linux/amd64
    k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubectl (static)
Env for linux/amd64: GOPATH=/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 GOROOT=/usr/local/go CGO_ENABLED= CC=
Coverage is disabled.
# cd /go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes; git status --porcelain
fatal: multi-pack-index version 2 not recognized
error obtaining VCS status: exit status 128
    Use -buildvcs=false to disable VCS stamping.
```

This is due to the host git using `multi-pack-index` version 2 while the build container git is too old to support this.

You can work around it in the short term like this:
```shell 
# cd to your kubernetes clone first, then run this:
rm .git/objects/pack/multi-pack-index
git fsck
```

Long-term we need to consider options to upgrade git in kube-cross.

### Which tests are failing?

`[sig-node] Summary API [NodeConformance] when querying /stats/summary should report resource usage through the stats api`

    Expected <uint64>: 0 to be >= <int>: 10000

```

### Since when has it been failing?

All available runs (90+) are failing, going back to at least `v1.36.0-alpha.0.647` (build 2011700799951867904).

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-containerd#cos-cgroupv2-containerd-node-e2e-alpha-features

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The job runs with `AllAlpha=true`, which enables `PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI=true`. This causes the kubelet to fetch stats via `ListPodSandboxStats` from containerd (built from main branch).

Containerd returns `UsageNanoCores` as a non-nil `UInt64Value{Value: 0}` rather than computing the actual value or leaving the field nil. Because the kubelet sees a non-nil value, it trusts it and bypasses its own cache-based delta computation (`cri_stats_provider.go:1002-1003`, `1026-1027`) that would correctly calculate nanocores from `UsageCoreNanoSeconds`.

The fix could be:
1. **containerd**: compute `UsageNanoCores` from the cgroup CPU delta, or leave the field nil so the kubelet's fallback kicks in.
2. **kubelet**: treat `UsageNanoCores.Value == 0` as "not provided" and fall through to the cache-based computation.

title: etcd watcher scalability or improve decode efficiency
body:
### What would you like to be added?

**Context**
We are developing a Custom Resource Definition (CRD) controller that utilizes the standard list-watch (informer) mechanism. Under high workload conditions, we are observing significant latency in the initial notification trigger for reconciliation loops.

**Observations**
Upon inspecting the Kubernetes API server logs, we identified a high volume of the following warning messages:

`"Fast watcher, slow processing. Probably caused by slow decoding, user not receiving fast, or other processing logic"
`

This suggests a bottleneck where the API server is generating events faster than they can be decoded or consumed. While the log message mentions "slow decoding," our monitoring indicates that the controller itself is not CPU-bound or busy; rather, it appears starved of events because the API server cannot push them efficiently.

**Current Investigation**
We noticed that starting in Kubernetes v1.31, the feature gate ConcurrentWatchObjectDecode was introduced to address decoding bottlenecks by parallelizing the decoding of watch events. However, the current implementation hardcodes the concurrency limit to 10 workers. And the incoming/outgoing bufSize are also hardcoded to 100.

We are seeking the guidance if we could increase the hardcoded settings to improve the watcher efficiency, and whether k8s could provide a feature or guidance how to tune this case, e.g. improve the decoding efficiency.

### Why is this needed?

The controller is being starved of timely updates because the API server cannot produce events efficiently.

title: apiserver: consistent read fallback to etcd can overload apiserver and etcd when watch cache is behind
body:
## What happened

When the watch cache is temporarily behind etcd for more than 3 seconds, a consistent LIST read that would normally be served from cache can fall back to a direct etcd LIST.

Relevant code paths:
- [watch cache 3s wait window](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L48-L53)
- [watch cache timeout returns [INLINE_CODE]](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/watch_cache.go#L446-L489)
- [consistent LIST fallback to etcd](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/delegator.go#L218-L224)

This becomes dangerous in degraded situations such as:
- etcd defragmentation
- leader re-election
- transient member stall
- delayed watch delivery

## Real-world impact

This failure mode was summarized well by @serathius:

> Consistent read from cache fallback, works great until defrag. 
> Defrag stalls member, watch gets delayed more than 3s, watch cache falls back reads to etcd. 
> Due to lack of APF protection (not aware of fallback), memory jumps, for 2GB pods resource we get: 
> Etcd 17GB->180GB 
> API server 50GB->160GB

This matches the current behavior: a request that is initially expected to be a cheap cache-backed consistent LIST read can become an expensive etcd LIST at runtime once the watch cache is still behind after the 3 second wait window.

## A graceful degradation may be safer

If the cache has not caught up within 3 seconds, etcd and/or apiserver are likely already under stress. In that situation, bypassing the cache and sending more expensive LIST traffic directly to etcd can make things much worse.

Kube-apiserver already has precedent for returning [INLINE_CODE] under degraded watch cache conditions. For example, when the watch cache is not ready, LIST requests can already be rejected with [INLINE_CODE]:
- [existing [INLINE_CODE] on unready watch cache](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L763-L768)

## Proposed direction

One possible direction would be to introduce a feature gate for this fallback path.

When enabled, if a consistent LIST read cannot be served from watch cache within the current 3 second wait window, kube-apiserver would return [INLINE_CODE] with [INLINE_CODE] instead of falling back to etcd. This would let clients retry later, rather than turning a cache-backed read into an expensive etcd LIST while the system is already degraded.

The reasoning is:
- if the cache is behind for more than 3 seconds, etcd and/or kube-apiserver are likely already under stress
- turning a cheap cache read into an expensive etcd LIST is risky
- asking clients to retry may give etcd time to recover and the watch cache time to catch up
- once the cache catches up again, the same consistent LIST can be served safely from cache

Using a feature gate would preserve backward compatibility and keep the current fallback-to-etcd behavior as the default, while allowing operators to opt into a safer graceful-degradation mode for large or sensitive clusters.

body_raw:
### What would you like to be added?

In release 1.36, we introduced initial changes to the Workload API (including `Workload` and `PodGroup` objects) in the `v1alpha2` version of the `scheduling.k8s.io` API group. For the 1.37 release, we plan to make further changes to these APIs and eventually promote them to Beta.
To follow Kubernetes API best practices and allow for breaking changes in the next iteration without maintaining multiple alpha versions, we need to create a new `v1alpha3` version as a copy of `v1alpha2`. We will migrate all internal consumers to `v1alpha3` and remove `v1alpha2` in this release. This avoids the overhead of maintaining both versions with conversion logic for an experimental API, while allowing us to evolve the API.

### Why is this needed?

We would like to promote the Workload API to `v1alpha3` and remove `v1alpha2` by performing the following steps:
1.  **Create `v1alpha3` API Definitions**:
    *   Copy `staging/src/k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3`.
    *   Copy `pkg/apis/scheduling/v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3`.
    *   Update package names and references to point to the new `v1alpha3`.
2.  **Remove `v1alpha2` API Definitions**:
    *   Delete the old `v1alpha2` directories in both `staging` and `pkg/apis`.
3.  **Update Internal References**:
    *   Update all imports and usages of `k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3` across the repository (e.g., in `pkg/scheduler/`, `plugin/pkg/admission/`).
4.  **Code Generation**:
    *   Run Kubernetes code generators to create clientsets, informers, listers, and deepcopy functions for the new version.

title: After switching the Go version to 1.26.1, the binary package has become significantly larger.
body:
### What happened?

The Kubernetes 1.34.1 code is used to compile a binary file using Go 1.24.6. The compilation command is as follows:
go build -ldflags "-s -w" -tags "grpcnotrace" -o _output/bin/kube-apiserver cmd/kube-apiserver/apiserver.go
Then, the binary file is compiled using Go 1.26.1. It is found that the size of the kube-apiserver binary file compiled using Go 1.24.6 is 85233956,
while the size of the kube-apiserver binary file compiled using Go 1.26.1 is 103235849, which is 18 MB larger than that of the binary file compiled using Go 1.24.6. This is unreasonable.
In addition, after I removed -tags "grpcnotrace", the size of the binary file compiled using Go 1.24.6 was 102572324, and the size of the binary file compiled using Go 1.26.1 was 103534857. That is, the -tags "grpcnotrace" option was very effective in Go 1.24.6, but had almost no effect in Go 1.26.1.

### What did you expect to happen?

The effect of -tags "grpcnotrace" should be the same in Go 1.26.1 and Go 1.24.6, and the binary size should not change significantly.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run the go build -ldflags "-s -w" -tags "grpcnotrace" -o _output/bin/kube-apiserver cmd/kube-apiserver/apiserver.go command to compile the binary file in go1.24.6 and go1.26.1, and then compare the sizes of the two binary files.

title: [Tracking] 5k scalability manual test (pull-kubernetes-gce-master-scale-performance-5000) is unstable
body:
The 5k manual scalability presubmit [INLINE_CODE]has been unstable over the last couple of days.

An apiserver restart test was added in https://github.com/kubernetes/perf-tests/pull/4013 and enabled on the 5k manual test on 5/16 (https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/37028), and every run afterwards has been failing.

## Known Issues

### (under investigation) kubelet lease renewal starvation on restart

https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/138758/pull-kubernetes-gce-master-scale-performance-5000/2057081218238779392 points to lease GET SLO violation. PUTs are unaffected.

### (fixed) coredns OOMKills on apiserver restart

Tracked in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/139117.

When the recently added apiserver-restart phase fires, ~75% of coredns pods are
OOMKilled because client-go's relist doubles the memory footprint, exceeding kops' 170Mi default limit.

### (fixed) Prow test-pod OOMKills

Tracked in https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/issues/37056

27GB is too small to support our scalability tests. Bump memory to 40GB for test runner pods. 

/sig scalability
/sig testing
/triage accepted

body_raw:
`TestLegacyServiceAccountTokenTracking` in `test/integration/serviceaccount/service_account_test.go` tries to tolerate the date changing while the test runs by capturing `dateBefore` and `dateAfter`, but the assertion currently requires the observed date to equal both values:

```go
if date != dateBefore || date != dateAfter {
    t.Fatalf("Secret was labeled with wrong date: %q", date)
}
```

The same pattern is used again for the ConfigMap check later in the test.

That condition only passes when `dateBefore == dateAfter == date`. If the test spans UTC midnight, `dateBefore != dateAfter`, so no valid value can satisfy the check and the test flakes even if the implementation is correct.

I think both checks should allow either boundary date instead:

```go
if date != dateBefore && date != dateAfter {
    ...
}
```

I traced this back to the original test added in commit `569cd70a52359a294a608fb256693445a89a9dab`, and it still exists after the later flake fix in commit `6784610bebedb33f22259042c728a798c1e04b03`, which changed the concurrency/warning-count part of the test but did not update these date assertions.

If this sounds right, I can put together a small PR that only fixes the two assertions.

body_raw:
### What happened?

When the Job controller's `manageJob()` function determines that replacement pods are needed but a backoff timer is active (due to recent pod failures), it returns `active=0` to the caller. The caller uses this value to set `job.Status.Active=0` in a status update, while `job.Status.Ready` retains the real informer-computed count. The apiserver validation `RejectMoreReadyThanActivePods` (GA in 1.33 via `JobManagedBy`) correctly rejects this inconsistent update with 422.

Because the status update fails, the controller cannot:
- Flush `uncountedTerminatedPods`
- Remove `batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking` finalizers from terminated pods

This causes pods to appear stuck in Terminating state and job status to become stale.

**Root cause:** Two locations in `manageJob()` return a hardcoded `0` instead of the real `active` count when backoff is active:

```go
// Location 1: global backoff
if remainingTime > 0 {
    jm.enqueueSyncJobWithDelay(logger, job, remainingTime)
    return 0, metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated, nil  // BUG: should be `active`
}

// Location 2: per-index backoff
if remainingTime > 0 {
    jm.enqueueSyncJobWithDelay(logger, job, remainingTime)
    return 0, metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated, nil  // BUG: should be `active`
}
```

The caller sets `job.Status.Active = active` (the returned 0), while `job.Status.Ready` stays at the informer count (e.g., 5). Result: `5 > 0` → 422.

The `0` was likely a "don't care" value from before `RejectMoreReadyThanActivePods` validation existed. Every other return path in `manageJob` returns the real active count.

### What did you expect to happen?

The backoff early-return in `manageJob()` should return the real active pod count (unchanged, since no pods were created or deleted), not 0.

Proposed fix:
```diff
     if remainingTime > 0 {
         jm.enqueueSyncJobWithDelay(logger, job, remainingTime)
-        return 0, metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated, nil
+        return active, metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated, nil
     }
```

Returning `active` (initialized at top of `manageJob` as `int32(len(jobCtx.activePods))`) means "I didn't create or delete any pods" — the correct semantics for a backoff deferral.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
# 1. Create a Job
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: repro-ready-active
  namespace: default
spec:
  parallelism: 30
  completions: 30
  backoffLimit: 500
  completionMode: Indexed
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "10m"
            memory: "16Mi"
EOF

# 2. Wait for all pods to be Running+Ready
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pods -l job-name=repro-ready-active --timeout=120s

# 3. Force-delete 25 pods simultaneously
kubectl get pods -l job-name=repro-ready-active -o name | head -25 | \
  xargs -P25 kubectl delete --force --grace-period=0

# 4. Observe: job status is frozen, KCM logs show error
kubectl get job repro-ready-active -o jsonpath='active={.status.active} ready={.status.ready} failed={.status.failed}'
# Output: active=30 ready=30 failed=   (stale — doesn't reflect reality)

# KCM logs show:
# "Unhandled Error" err="syncing job: tracking status: adding uncounted pods to status:
#   Job.batch \"repro-ready-active\" is invalid: status.ready: Invalid value: 5:
#   cannot set more ready pods than active"

# 5. Bug self-resolves after ~10 min when backoff expires (if no new failures arrive)
```

### Anything else we need to know?

- The bug fires on any multi-pod Job that experiences a pod failure while other pods are still Ready. For single failures (10s backoff), it produces a few 422 errors that self-resolve. For mass failures (spot reclamation, node failure → backoff capped at 10 min), it causes visible stuck pods and stale status for the full backoff duration.
- No data loss occurs. The job eventually completes. The impact is operational: stuck Terminating pods, stale status, KCM error log spam.
- The `metrics.JobSyncActionPodsCreated` label on the return is also incorrect (no pods were created), but that's cosmetic.


### Kubernetes version

<details>

Bug present from 1.31 (when `RejectMoreReadyThanActivePods` was introduced, beta default-on) through latest master. Unconditional from 1.33 (`JobManagedBy` GA).

Tested and reproduced on 1.35.


</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
AWS (EKS), but not cloud-specific. Reproducible on any cluster.
</details>

N/A

N/A

_No response_

title: [Feature Request] Native Zone/Topology-Aware Scaling in HPA to complement Topology Aware Routing
body:
### What would you like to be added?

### Description
When combining **Topology Aware Routing** ([INLINE_CODE]) with the **HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA)**, there is a systemic architectural gap that risks localized pod starvation during scale-out events, and extreme endpoint imbalance during scale-in events. 

Currently, the HPA evaluates resource utilization (e.g., CPU, Memory) as a global, deployment-wide aggregate average. However, Topology Aware Routing deliberately isolates traffic to localized Availability Zones (AZs). 

This decoupled behavior creates a "Thundering Herd" trap during spikes, and a "Starvation" trap during downscaling, because the network routing layer is highly topology-aware while the autoscaling control loop is completely topology-blind.

### Why is this needed?

### Use Case
We run high-throughput microservices on AWS (EKS) distributed across 3 Availability Zones. To mitigate high cross-AZ data transfer costs ("Cross-AZ Tax") and lower network latency, we rely heavily on Topology Aware Routing. 

We face two distinct structural failures due to the lack of zone-aware autoscaling:

1. **The Scale-Out Trap (Localized Overload):** During localized network shifts or zone-specific traffic spikes, pods in a single AZ (e.g., [INLINE_CODE]) take 100% of that localized load. If [INLINE_CODE] pods hit 95% CPU utilization while pods in [INLINE_CODE] and [INLINE_CODE] remain idle at 10%, the cluster-wide average sits at ~38%. The HPA fails to trigger, and the pods in the stressed zone crash due to localized resource starvation.
2. **The Scale-In Trap (Zone Depletion):** When traffic drops globally and the HPA triggers a downscale event, the underlying ReplicaSet controller selects pods for termination without respecting zone distribution. It frequently terminates a disproportionate number of pods from a single zone. This leaves that specific zone entirely depleted of endpoints, breaking the path for subsequent localized traffic and forcing expensive, high-latency cross-AZ failovers.

### Proposed Solution / Architectural Approaches
We request native support for zone/topology-awareness within the core autoscaling and lifecycle framework:

1. **Topology-Aware Scale-Out Policy:** Introduce a configuration field in the HPA spec (e.g., [INLINE_CODE]) that evaluates metrics per topology domain. If *any single zone* breaches the target utilization threshold, the HPA should proactively trigger a scale-up event.
2. **Topology-Aware Scale-In (Downscaling):** Ensure that when the HPA reduces the replica count, the scale-in mechanism balances pod terminations proportionally across all active topology domains. The controller must prevent downscaling from leaving a specific zone starved of healthy endpoints.
3. **Handling Soft Constraints ([INLINE_CODE]):** If a deployment utilizes [INLINE_CODE], a Zone-Aware HPA should exploit this flexibility. During a localized spike, it should scale up replicas specifically within the hurting topology domain, allowing a temporary skew to absorb the traffic. During the subsequent scale-in event, the controller must prioritize deleting pods from the skewed zone to automatically return the cluster to its baseline balanced topology spread.

### Related Existing Issue
* **kubernetes/kubernetes #124149** 

### Additional Context
Current ecosystem workarounds require engineers to deploy entirely independent, duplicated Deployments and HPAs per AZ (e.g., [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE]). This completely breaks standard GitOps principles, bloat CI/CD pipelines, and forces rigid, static replica constraints. Native lifecycle zone-awareness is required to bridge the gap between how Kubernetes routes traffic and how it manages compute capacity.

### What happened?

When creating a Binding object with invalid or incomplete `target` fields, the API Server returns HTTP 500.

For example, when `target.kind` is unsupported and `target.name` is missing, the response is:

```json
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "[target.kind: Unsupported value: \"foo\": supported values: \"Node\", \"<empty>\", target.name: Required value]",
  "code": 500
}
```
A similar HTTP 500 response can also be triggered when target.name is missing. These look like validation failures in the request body and should not be reported as internal server errors.

### What did you expect to happen?

The API Server should return a 4xx validation response, such as HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity, instead of HTTP 500.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Start a Kubernetes cluster with an affected version.
2. Start a local API proxy:

```bash
kubectl proxy --port=8001
```
3. Send the following request:
Case 1: unsupported `target.kind` and missing `target.name`:

```bash
curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/namespaces/default/bindings' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"target":{"kind":"foo"}}'
```
Case 2: missing target.name:
```bash
curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/namespaces/default/bindings' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"target":{}}'
```
Both requests return HTTP 500 in my test environment.

### Anything else we need to know?

This issue was found by fuzzing Kubernetes RESTful APIs. I reproduced it on Kubernetes 1.33.1 and 1.36.0.

### What happened?

A pod using a CSI volume with `volumeMount.subPath` got stuck in `Terminating`.

The workload container had already exited, but kubelet repeatedly failed during volume cleanup before calling CSI `NodeUnpublishVolume`.

Example kubelet logs:

```text
UnmountVolume started for volume "<pvc-name>" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/csi/<driver>^<volume>")
Warning: mount cleanup skipped because path does not exist:
/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<pod-uid>/volume-subpaths/<volume-name>/xxxx/3

Warning: mount cleanup skipped because path does not exist:
/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<pod-uid>/volume-subpaths/<volume-name>/xxxx/5

Operation ... failed. No retries permitted until ...
Error: error cleaning subPath mounts for volume "<pvc-name>" ...
error deleting /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<pod-uid>/volume-subpaths/<volume-name>/xxxx:
remove .../xxxx: directory not empty
```
### What did you expect to happen?

If a subPath target path returns ENOENT but the mount is still present in mountinfo, kubelet should not skip cleanup and then fail on the parent directory with directory not empty.

Kubelet should either detect the stale/deleted mountpoint from mountinfo and attempt to unmount it, or re-check/re-walk remaining subPath entries before failing the parent directory removal.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We do not yet have a manifest-only reproducer. The key failure state is:

```text
a kubelet subPath bind target is still present in mountinfo,
but stat(2) on the subPath target returns ENOENT

title: EasyCLA blocks website main to dev branch-sync PRs on kubernetes-prow[bot] merge commits
body:
### What happened?

Weekly "Merge main branch into dev-1.37" sync PRs against [INLINE_CODE] fail the **EasyCLA** check with [INLINE_CODE], and the only committer flagged is the bot identity [INLINE_CODE].

These sync PRs merge [INLINE_CODE] into the release dev branch, which by design pulls in the merge commits that Prow created when merging earlier PRs. EasyCLA evaluates every commit author in the PR, finds the [INLINE_CODE]-authored merge commits, and reports them as not covered by a signed CLA. Every human contributor on the branch passes; only the bot fails.

Key detail: in the same EasyCLA report, the older bot identity **[INLINE_CODE] (name "Kubernetes Prow Robot") passes** the CLA check, while the newer GitHub App identity **[INLINE_CODE] fails**. So merge commits that used to be authored by the CLA-authorized [INLINE_CODE] are now authored by [INLINE_CODE], which has no CLA association - that identity change appears to be what newly breaks these sync PRs.

Examples:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/56271 — EasyCLA [INLINE_CODE]. [INLINE_CODE] ✅ (e.g. [INLINE_CODE]), but [INLINE_CODE] ❌ (35 merge commits, e.g. [INLINE_CODE]).
- https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/56300 — fresh sync PR, same failure on the same bot identity.

This blocks the routine weekly branch sync during the v1.37 cycle: [INLINE_CODE] reports "Not mergeable. Needs ... cncf-cla: yes" because the bot commits aren't CLA-authorized.

### What did you expect to happen?

Merge commits authored by [INLINE_CODE] that arrive via a [INLINE_CODE] → [INLINE_CODE] sync merge should not block EasyCLA / the [INLINE_CODE] label - the same way the older [INLINE_CODE] identity is already treated - so the routine weekly branch sync can proceed.

Rebasing/squashing is not a viable fix here: the entire purpose of the sync PR is to carry [INLINE_CODE]'s merge history into the dev branch, so dropping those bot merge commits would defeat the sync. ### What happened?

When kubelet runs an HTTP liveness/readiness/startup probe, it logs probe parameters at verbosity `-v=4` — and the logged fields include the raw `HTTPGet.HTTPHeaders` values taken directly from the PodSpec:

```go
// pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go:160-173
case p.HTTPGet != nil:
    req, err := httpprobe.NewRequestForHTTPGetAction(p.HTTPGet, &container, status.PodIP, "probe")
    if err != nil {
        logger.V(4).Info("HTTP-Probe failed to create request", "error", err)
        return probe.Unknown, "", err
    }
    if loggerV4 := logger.V(4); logger.Enabled() {
        port := req.URL.Port()
        host := req.URL.Hostname()
        path := req.URL.Path
        scheme := req.URL.Scheme
        headers := p.HTTPGet.HTTPHeaders              // <-- raw PodSpec headers
        loggerV4.Info("HTTP-Probe", "scheme", scheme, "host", host, "port", port,
            "path", path, "timeout", timeout, "headers", headers, "probeType", probeType)  // <-- sink
    }
    return pb.http.Probe(req, timeout)
```

`headers := p.HTTPGet.HTTPHeaders` is the user-supplied header list with **no redaction**, emitted into the `"headers"` structured field.

### What did you expect to happen?

The kubelet prober should not log raw probe `httpHeaders`. The `"headers"` field should be dropped or redacted (e.g. log only header names, or omit the value) in the `HTTP-Probe` line at `prober.go:173` — matching how other secret-bearing probe fields are handled. As written, attacker/operator-supplied credential headers are emitted verbatim into verbose logs.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

copy-paste into a shell **inside the kubernetes repo** (auto-detects root). It drops a same-package Go test under `pkg/kubelet/prober`, sets `-v=4`, builds an HTTP liveness probe with `Authorization: Bearer kubelet-probe-secret-token`, calls the real `(*prober).runProbe`, and the fake HTTP prober returns `Success` — proving the leak happens **before** the request executes and does not require probe failure. Cleans up after itself; no cluster needed.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
F="$ROOT/pkg/kubelet/prober/zz_poc_probe_header_leak_test.go"
SECRET="Bearer kubelet-probe-secret-token"
trap 'rm -f "$F"' EXIT
cat >"$F" <<'GOEOF'
package prober

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	v1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr"
	kubecontainer "k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/container"
	"k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/probe"
	"k8s.io/klog/v2"
)

type pocSuccessHTTPProber struct{}

func (pocSuccessHTTPProber) Probe(_ *http.Request, _ time.Duration) (probe.Result, string, error) {
	return probe.Success, "ok", nil // probe SUCCEEDS — leak is pre-request, not failure-only
}

func TestPOCHTTPProbeHeaderLogLeak(t *testing.T) {
	if flag.CommandLine.Lookup("v") == nil {
		klog.InitFlags(nil)
	}
	if err := flag.Set("v", "4"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	pb := &prober{http: pocSuccessHTTPProber{}}
	_, _, err := pb.runProbe(
		context.Background(),
		liveness,
		&v1.Probe{ProbeHandler: v1.ProbeHandler{HTTPGet: &v1.HTTPGetAction{
			Path: "/healthz",
			Port: intstr.FromInt32(8080),
			HTTPHeaders: []v1.HTTPHeader{
				{Name: "Authorization", Value: "Bearer kubelet-probe-secret-token"},
			},
		}}},
		&v1.Pod{},
		v1.PodStatus{PodIP: "127.0.0.1"},
		v1.Container{Name: "app"},
		kubecontainer.ContainerID{Type: "test", ID: "container"},
	)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	klog.Flush()
}
GOEOF
OUT="$( cd "$ROOT" && go test ./pkg/kubelet/prober -run TestPOCHTTPProbeHeaderLogLeak -count=1 -v 2>&1 )"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep 'HTTP-Probe' || true
if printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -F "$SECRET"; then
  echo "VULNERABLE: kubelet HTTP probe Authorization header leaked into verbose logs"
else
  echo "NOT VULNERABLE: secret header not observed in logs" >&2; exit 1
fi
```

Expected: a `prober.go` `HTTP-Probe` log line containing the secret in the `headers` field, followed by the `VULNERABLE` confirmation:

```text
I0702 11:32:34.631974 2674209 prober.go:173] "HTTP-Probe" scheme="http" host="127.0.0.1" port="8080" path="/healthz" timeout="0s" headers=[{"name":"Authorization","value":"Bearer kubelet-probe-secret-token"}] probeType="Liveness"
VULNERABLE: kubelet HTTP probe Authorization header leaked into verbose logs
```

### Anything else we need to know?

- This is secret disclosure of probe-configured credentials to kubelet verbose logs. It is a duplicate of the same finding already recorded internally as `kubelet_prober_http_probe_header_log_leak`.
- It is **distinct** from the recorded `kubelet_http_probe_header_log_leak` (sink `pkg/probe/http/http.go:119`, failure-only). This report's sink is `pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go:173` (pre-request), so successful probes leak too. Both are already separately recorded in the knowledge base.
- Affects HTTP liveness/readiness/startup probes; requires kubelet `-v>=4`. `TCP`/`Exec`/`GRPC` probes do not carry `httpHeaders` at this sink.

title: Watch client shutdown: three remaining bugs from #131505
body:
In 2025 I fixed several watch client shutdown bugs: #131266 (reflector Stop deadlock), #131321 (VeryShortWatchError), #131706 (watch test body cleanup). Thanks again to @wojtek-t and @liggitt for those reviews.

The test work in #131505 turned up three more bugs. They were documented there as TODOs but never fixed. I've verified all three still exist on master (843726939e9) and plan to send one small PR per bug:

1. **Response body leak.** [INLINE_CODE] doesn't close [INLINE_CODE] when content-type negotiation fails. Tracked in #140464.

2. **Error event after Stop.** [INLINE_CODE] selects between the done channel and the error send. When both are ready Go picks at random, so a decode error racing with [INLINE_CODE] reaches the consumer about half the time. First reported back in 2015 (#6433) and again recently in #139782. The open fix #139783 adds the http2 error string to [INLINE_CODE], which helps that case, but the race allows any decode error through after Stop. My PR will check the done channel first so a stopped watcher just closes its result channel.

3. **Broken error unwrapping.** [INLINE_CODE] and the client watch decoder wrap decode errors with [INLINE_CODE], which severs [INLINE_CODE]/[INLINE_CODE]. Consumers end up string-matching the message. Config Sync, for example, matches the literal "unable to decode an event from the watch stream: context canceled" text to detect shutdown. Small enough to fix without its own issue.

Each PR is small, structured as a failing test commit followed by the fix, with race detector and stress output in the description.

Requesting [INLINE_CODE] so the fix PRs land against accepted issues.

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery

title: Remove the retired Go Report Card badge from README
body:
**What happened**

The README still shows a Go Report Card badge. Go Report Card has been sunset — https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes now returns a retirement notice instead of a grade, so the badge no longer links to anything meaningful.

**What you expected to happen**

README badges point to live services.

**Anything else we need to know?**

Proposal: drop the badge from README.md. The upstream site recommends golangci-lint, which this repo already runs in CI.

/sig contributor-experience
/kind cleanup

title: HPA shows integer underflow value (-9223372036854775808m) for AverageValue metric targets when replicas is 0
body:
### What happened?

When a workload is scaled down to 0 replicas (with KEDA for instance), the HPA controller attempts to calculate the average metric value (total metric / 0 replicas). This division by zero causes the HPA's [INLINE_CODE] to underflow to [INLINE_CODE](math.MinInt64) and, if the scaling becomes then inactive, gets stuck with this underflow value in the HPA object.

### What did you expect to happen?

When the workload replica count is 0, skip the per-pod average calculation. The HPA controller should bypass the division step when statusReplicas == 0 and return the total raw metric value as a fallback.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Configure an HPA with an External metric and target type AverageValue
- Scale the workload up to at least 1 replica so the HPA performs a metric evaluation
- Scale the workload down to 0 replicas
- Check the HPA status using kubectl get hpa (or -o yaml)

I have made a script to reproduce this with KEDA in https://gist.github.com/KengoA/65599c5ffd635c5e1c1c783502a7d340 which I ran on a GKE cluster. I have the full stdout from the script in the gist, but it gets into a state like the following (replicas is shown as 5 here when I printed the output but this becomes 0 after a few seconds):
[CODE_BLOCK]

This is also reported in https://github.com/kedacore/keda/issues/5730 with other users facing a similar issue, and the overflow/underflow issue is identified by in https://github.com/kedacore/keda/issues/5730#issuecomment-2247692693.

### Anything else we need to know?

The zero division and then underflow issue seems to happen on GKE clusters which I replicated above. I saw moments of overflow during transient phases.

title: gofmt in go1.26.5 gives different output on amd64 and arm64, which breaks ci-kubernetes-verify-master-canary
body:
### Which jobs are failing?

ci-kubernetes-verify-master-canary (the only verify job that runs on arm64 nodes, on the AKS build cluster)

### Which tests are failing?

verify-gofmt.sh

### Since when has it been failing?

First failure 2026-07-20 17:12 UTC, a few hours after #140000 merged. The job then alternated between green and red depending on which node it landed on. It has failed every run since 2026-07-29 17:06 UTC because every pod since then has landed on arm64 nodes.

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-k8s-infra-canaries#verify-master-canary

### Reason for failure (if possible)

gofmt from go1.26.5 does not produce the same output on amd64 and arm64 for one struct literal in [INLINE_CODE] (added in #140000). The amd64 build of gofmt accepts the code as checked in. The arm64 build wants the short fields aligned to the long [INLINE_CODE] line. Each build rejects the form the other one wants, so running update-gofmt cannot produce a form both accept.

This is a bug in Go, not in the release binaries. The gofmt binaries in the CI image match the official go.dev tarballs, and building gofmt from unmodified go1.26.5 sources reproduces the difference purely by changing GOARCH. The cause is in go/printer, which decides where to break column alignment using a geometric mean computed with [INLINE_CODE] and [INLINE_CODE] (nodes.go lines 232 to 287 in go1.26.5). Those functions can differ in the last bit between architectures, and the field lengths in this literal sit exactly on the 2.5 ratio threshold, so the decision flips. Presubmits run on amd64, which is why the change merged cleanly.

Evidence: the last green run (build 2082497666687700992, amd64 node) and the first red run of the streak (build 2082513014723973120, arm64 node) tested the same commit 7fbcad5e8ec.

### Anything else we need to know?

The fix on our side is to restructure the literal so the long field is assigned after the struct is built. I verified that form is accepted by gofmt from go1.26.5 on linux amd64, linux arm64, and darwin arm64, and by go1.27rc2. I will send a PR and file a golang/go issue for the printer bug.

cc @natasha41575 @BenTheElder

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig k8s-infra
/sig scheduling
/kind failing-test

body:
What happened?

hack/README.md has several writing quality issues:

Line 8 — "many" is a weasel word that weakens meaning
Lines 15–16 — Comma splice: "redirection, Please" — "Please" starts a new sentence and should not be joined with a comma
Lines 15 & 17 — "It is equivalent" is wordy phrasing
Line 17 — Missing space: ".It is"
Line 20 — Passive voice: "must be run" — could be rewritten in active voice

title: Kubernetes ships etcd 3.6.6-0 with 61 CVEs (2 Critical) across all supported versions — upstream 3.7.1 available
body:
/sig cluster-lifecycle
/sig etcd
/kind bug
/priority critical-urgent

## Summary

All currently supported Kubernetes versions (v1.34.x, v1.35.x, v1.36.x)
ship [INLINE_CODE], which contains **61 known
vulnerabilities** in the etcd binary alone including **2 Critical**.
The upstream etcd project has released v3.7.1.

etcd 3.6.6-0 has the **oldest dependencies of any Kubernetes control
plane component**, compiled with Go 1.24.10 and gRPC 1.71.1.

## Confirmed Across All Supported K8s Versions
[CODE_BLOCK]

## Scan Results
[CODE_BLOCK]

## CRITICAL Vulnerabilities

| CVE | Library | Installed | Fixed | Title |
|-----|---------|-----------|-------|-------|
| CVE-2026-33186 | google.golang.org/grpc | **v1.71.1** | 1.79.3 | **gRPC-Go: Authorization bypass due to improper HTTP/2 path validation** |
| CVE-2025-68121 | Go stdlib | **v1.24.10** | 1.24.13 | **Incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption** |

**Both are directly exploitable in etcd:**
- etcd IS a gRPC server — gRPC is its primary communication protocol
- etcd uses mTLS for peer-to-peer and client communication

## etcd-Specific CVEs 

etcd 3.6.6 has additional CVEs due to its older Go stdlib (1.24.10):

| CVE | Severity | Title |
|-----|----------|-------|
| CVE-2025-61726 | HIGH | Memory exhaustion in net/url query parameter parsing |
| CVE-2025-61729 | HIGH | DoS via excessive resource consumption in crypto/x509 |
| CVE-2025-61727 | MEDIUM | x509 subdomain constraint doesn't restrict wildcard SANs |
| CVE-2025-61728 | MEDIUM | Excessive CPU in archive/zip |
| CVE-2025-61730 | MEDIUM | TLS handshake messages at incorrect encryption level |
| CVE-2025-47913 | HIGH | SSH client panic (x/crypto 0.36.0 specific) |
| CVE-2025-47914 | MEDIUM | SSH Agent DoS via malformed messages |
| CVE-2025-58181 | MEDIUM | DoS via unbounded GSSAPI memory consumption |
| CVE-2025-47911 | MEDIUM | Quadratic HTML parsing complexity |
| CVE-2025-58190 | MEDIUM | Infinite HTML parsing loop |

## Impact

etcd stores **all Kubernetes cluster state** including secrets,
configmaps, RBAC policies, and service accounts. A compromise of
etcd means complete cluster compromise. The CRITICAL gRPC
authorization bypass (CVE-2026-33186) and TLS certificate
validation failure (CVE-2025-68121) in the component that guards
all cluster data is an urgent concern.

## Request

1. **Bump etcd to 3.7.1** (or latest compatible) in upcoming
 patch releases for v1.35.x and v1.36.x
2. If 3.7.x has compatibility concerns, at minimum bump to a
 newer 3.6.x patch (if one exists with updated dependencies)
3. Is there a tracking issue for etcd version updates?

## How to Reproduce

```bash
trivy image registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.6-0

title: DeviceTaintRule with deviceSelector omitted blocks device allocation cluster-wide, including adminAccess claims, contradicting documented behavior
body:
### What happened?

A [INLINE_CODE] with the [INLINE_CODE] field entirely omitted (not an empty [INLINE_CODE] object
-- the field itself absent) makes every device on every node, across every driver and pool,
untolerated and therefore unschedulable -- not just whatever devices the taint was meant to
target.

Live-verified on a freshly-created kind cluster running v1.37.0 GA with **no non-default
feature gates set at all** ([INLINE_CODE]/[INLINE_CODE]/[INLINE_CODE]
are all GA and enabled by default at this release):

1. An ordinary [INLINE_CODE] targeting one device ([INLINE_CODE]) allocates and its Pod runs, with
 zero [INLINE_CODE]s present.
2. Apply a [INLINE_CODE] with [INLINE_CODE] and [INLINE_CODE] omitted:
 [CODE_BLOCK]
3. The exact same claim/Pod from step 1, recreated, now fails to schedule ([INLINE_CODE],
 [INLINE_CODE]).
4. Also confirmed on a 4-device pool: every device becomes unschedulable, not just one --
 including a claim declaring [INLINE_CODE], which is otherwise documented to bypass
 ordinary device exclusivity but is not exempted from [INLINE_CODE] enforcement.
5. Deleting only the [INLINE_CODE] (no other change) immediately restores every
 previously-blocked claim to allocate successfully.

### What did you expect to happen?

According to the field's own documentation ([INLINE_CODE]):

> The empty selector matches all devices. Without a selector, no devices are matches [sic].

A [INLINE_CODE] with [INLINE_CODE] omitted should match **zero** devices and have no
scheduling effect -- the opposite of what actually happens.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a cluster running v1.37.0 (no special feature gates required).
2. Install any DRA driver advertising at least one device (repro used
 [INLINE_CODE] v0.4.0).
3. Create an ordinary [INLINE_CODE] + Pod referencing one device; confirm it runs.
4. Apply a [INLINE_CODE] with any [INLINE_CODE] and [INLINE_CODE] omitted entirely.
5. Observe: any *new* claim against *any* device in the cluster -- including unrelated
 drivers/pools, and [INLINE_CODE] claims -- fails to schedule.
6. Delete the [INLINE_CODE]; confirm previously-blocked claims immediately allocate.

### Anything else we need to know?

- This appears specific to the [INLINE_CODE] enforcement path. Tested [INLINE_CODE] separately: a
 [INLINE_CODE] [INLINE_CODE] with [INLINE_CODE] omitted does **not** evict an already-running
 pod on an unrelated device (its [INLINE_CODE] condition stays [INLINE_CODE]
 indefinitely) -- confirmed the eviction mechanism itself works correctly in the same environment
 via a positive control (a [INLINE_CODE] taint with a matching selector evicted the target pod
 within 5 seconds). So the nil-selector matching bug looks confined to whatever code path
 [INLINE_CODE] uses to block new allocation, not the separate eviction controller.
- Distinct from #141422 / the pending fix in #141425: that issue concerns a selector that is
 *present but empty* ([INLINE_CODE]). This report is about the field being *absent*
 entirely -- confirmed by reading #141425's diff that its new validation only rejects the
 empty-but-present case and returns immediately with no error when the selector is nil, so it
 does not cover this scenario.
- Creating a [INLINE_CODE] is a cluster-scoped permission not granted by any built-in
 [INLINE_CODE]/[INLINE_CODE]/[INLINE_CODE] ClusterRole -- but this bug means anyone holding that permission can
 silently take down DRA scheduling cluster-wide with one missing field, when the documented
 default behavior should be a no-op.
